interval exponential/log routines and rational Machin pi, not primary code.

## S1. A general constant-preserving stability map preserves norm floors

Suppose a complex-linear map T on a finite polynomial space fixes constants
and maps EVERY closed-polydisc zero-free polynomial in that space to a
closed-polydisc zero-free polynomial. If m=min_D |f|>0, then for EVERY
complex lambda with |lambda|<m, f-lambda is in the same space and zero-free.
Thus Tf-lambda is zero-free. Tf avoids the open disk of radius m at EVERY
point of the closed polydisc, and min_D|Tf|>=m. This statement requires
stability of f-lambda too, not just stability of one supplied f. All maps
below meet that condition. Subtracting a constant never enlarges degree.

## S2. Pair averaging proves the polarization fact we need

For |u|,|v|<1 the symmetric multi-affine quadratic polarization

  Q(z,w)=1+(u+v)*(z+w)/2+u*v*z*w

is zero-free on the closed bidisk. To prove it put b=(u+v)/2,d=u*v.
For |z|=1 the squared denominator-minus-numerator when solving for w is

  |1+b*z|^2-|b+d*z|^2
    =1-|d|^2+2*Re((b-conj(b)*d)*z).

Now2*(b-conj(b)*d)=u*(1-|v|^2)+v*(1-|u|^2), whose modulus is at most
(|u|+|v|)*(1-|u*v|). The strict remaining reserve is at least

  (1-|u*v|)*(1-|u|)*(1-|v|)>0.

Also |b|<1, so the denominator1+b*z has no zero on the closed disk.

as a+b*z+c*w+d*z*w. The diagonal a+(b+c)*zeta+d*zeta^2 is stable because

 a*(1+u*zeta)*(1+v*zeta), |u|,|v|<1, allowing zero factors. The result
above proves its polarization

is stable. This is exactly the pair average E_ij f=(f+swap_ij f)/2.
Consequently every pair average preserves full closed-polydisc stability;
by S1 it also preserves the same positive minimum modulus.

For any disk-stable one-variable q of degree n, factor
q(z)=a0*product_(i=1)^n(1+u_i*z), |u_i|<1. Its multi-affine product
f(z_1,...,z_n)=a0*product(1+u_i*z_i) is stable with minimum at least
|a0|*product(1-|u_i|)>0. Repeatedly cycle through a finite set of pair
transpositions generating all permutations and replace f by E_ij f.

the common fixed subspace (symmetric coefficient arrays). Its orthogonal
complement is invariant under each projection. The norm of their product
